nodes.label: Page transitions
nodes.choice: Cross-document View Transitions, CSS only
nodes.text: Page transitions Cross-document View Transitions, CSS only `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` with a root cross-fade of 120 ms (≤ 150 ms), declared only inside `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` so reduced-motion readers get none. nodes.label: Prefetch
nodes.choice: Speculation Rules `prefetch`, moderate eagerness; never prerender
nodes.text: Prefetch Speculation Rules `prefetch`, moderate eagerness; never prerender One JSON `<script type="speculationrules">` (`src/lib/speculation-rules.ts`) in every page head: same-origin links only, excluding `#` links, `target=_blank`, `download`, `rel=external` and file paths. Astro's own prefetch script is off (`prefetch: false`), so every page ships one fewer script. Prerender is forbidden: it would run page code, and later analytics (§11), before the visit. Chromium only; Safari and Firefox navigate normally, so no request is spent on pages that may not be read.
nodes.consequence: One JSON `<script type="speculationrules">` (`src/lib/speculation-rules.ts`) in every page head: same-origin links only, excluding `#` links, `target=_blank`, `download`, `rel=external` and file paths. nodes.label: Lesson step-by-step figures
nodes.choice: CSS-only, learner-controlled steppers in lesson figures (owner decisions, 2026-11-18; auto-play dropped for the data steppers after research issue #58; autoplay concept animations added by owner request the same day)
nodes.text: Lesson step-by-step figures CSS-only, learner-controlled steppers in lesson figures (owner decisions, 2026-11-18; auto-play dropped for the data steppers after research issue #58; autoplay concept animations added by owner request the same day) A figure may show a concept where rows move (aggregation, grouping, joins, windows, CTE pipelines, set operations, recursion) as at most 6 steps the learner advances: controls Back, 1 to N, Next (44 px tall targets, keyboard arrows, visible focus). It is an inline SVG built at build time by `scripts/make-animation.mjs` from our own lesson rows, styled by `src/styles/step-animation.css`. The controls are a native radio group with labels (`<input type="radio">`, `<label>`), and the checked radio selects the state through sibling selectors (`.rK:checked ~ svg .iN`): zero JavaScript, no library, no `:has()` (lessons still ship no JS beyond D31). Step…
nodes.consequence: A figure may show a concept where rows move (aggregation, grouping, joins, windows, CTE pipelines, set operations, recursion) as at most 6 steps the learner advances: controls Back, 1 to N, Next (44 px tall targets, keyboard arrows, visible focus). It is an inline SVG built at build time by `scripts/make-animation.mjs` from our own lesson rows, styled by `src/styles/step-animation.css`. The controls are a native radio group with labels (`<input type="radio">`, `<label>`), and the checked radio selects the state through sibling selectors (`.rK:checked ~ svg .iN`): zero JavaScript, no library, no `:has()` (lessons still ship no JS beyond D31). Step 1 is the default view; each step changes one thing, runs a 0.45 s opacity transition from the previous state (none for reduced motion, the steps still switch), and Back works. Under the figure all step captions stay on the page as a numbered list, the current one marked; each starts with a clause badge, and a caption before a revealing step carries a "Predict:" prompt that does not give the result away (captions state operations, not the numbers a step reveals). One fixed color per SQL clause role (FROM/JOIN, ON, WHERE/HAVING, GROUP BY, SELECT/aggregates, OVER, ORDER BY; seven color-blind-safe hues, each at least 3:1 on both pure black and pure white), used only inside figures; groups inside one role are shade steps, and labels and numbers always stay. Print and any reader that ignores the radios get the static storyboard: the final frame plus all captions, without controls. Each figure stays under about 15 KB of markup. Original work drawn from our own data; GIF, WebP and a user-switched color mode were rejected, and so was auto-play for these data steppers. No new authoring component: plain `<figure>`, `<svg>`, `<input>` and `<label>` markup (§6). Concept animations (owner request, 2026-11-18): a lesson may also carry abstract, schematic, autoplay looping diagrams that explain an idea with no real data (rows are plain boxes with labels such as Row 1, Col 3, t1, Σ; aggregate against window, kinds of CTE, join types, the logical order of a query). They are CSS keyframes only, no JavaScript: a loop of 4 to 8 s in 8 phases that holds its final state for about a second before repeating, one animation per figure with a short caption under it. A native checkbox styled as a 44 px Pause / Play button stops every animation in the figure through a sibling selector (WCAG 2.2.2, because they play longer than 5 s). Step buttons (owner request, 2026-11-18): next to Pause sit Back, Next and one button per step ("1 2 3 … N", N = 3 to 6 distinct steps, each saying in plain words what changes), a native radio group `[auto, 1..N]` with the radios in the flow like the data steppers (no JavaScript, no `:has()`); choosing a step stops the loop and draws the settled frame at the end of that step's last phase from the same markup (each part carries its delay `--d`, the step sets `--off` and every animation is paused), and Play returns to autoplay; the in-figure label and the numbered caption list under the figure use the same words, with the current one marked, each radio is labeled "Step k of N: caption", arrow keys move between steps. Reduced motion shows step 1, still, and the buttons switch frames instantly; print shows the final state, all captions and no controls. Same clause colors and generator (`loop` option, specs `scripts/animations/concept-*.mjs`); about 5 KB of markup each, the CSS is shared. They go at the top of a lesson's "How it works" section. Never text over text at any moment of the loop. Live counts and Key idea (owner decision, 2026-11-19; piloted on three data steppers and five concept animations, then rolled out the same day to every concept animation and the three data steppers: all carry a Key idea, and all but `concept-cte-kinds` also a strip): both figure types may carry two optional additions, CSS only, no JavaScript, written by the generator from optional spec fields (a spec without them renders exactly as before). (1) A count strip of up to 5 small labeled counters above the picture (`counts: [{ label, value, role }]` per step, `counters: [{ label, role, values: [[phase, text]] }]` for concept animations): each shows "—" until its step, shows the number of rows at that step (for example `rows 10`, `groups 3`, `after HAVING 2`, or `FROM 7`, `WHERE 5`, `GROUP BY 3`, `HAVING 2`, `LIMIT 1`), and the counters set at the current step are lit in their clause color (a step that covers several phases keeps them lit to its end). (2) Under the controls a Key idea panel for the current step only: one plain sentence of at most 110 characters (`key`) and up to 3 What changed chips (`changes: [['+', 'column orders'], ['−', '1 row dropped'], ['~', 'rows reordered']]`; the sign is drawn by CSS and spoken as Added, Removed, Changed). The panel holds the text of every step in one grid cell, so its height is that of the tallest and nothing below it moves. In a stepper the checked radio selects the counter state and the panel item (`visibility`, no `:has()`); in a concept animation the counters and the panel use the same keyframes as the picture, so they follow the phases in autoplay and a step button shows them at the end of its last phase (and the strip and panel are `aria-hidden` there, because the captions and step labels already carry the words). Nothing spoils a Predict: a count, key idea or change appears only at the step that shows it, and step 1 shows inputs only; numbers in the data steppers were recomputed with DuckDB 2.0.0 on cafe-sales. Print shows the final counter values and, as a block before the caption list, every step's Key idea and What changed, numbered `Step 1 · key idea` by a CSS counter (the live panel itself keeps one copy of each text, so nothing is written twice); reduced motion shows step 1 and the steps switch instantly, with no animation of the counters. Our own look: Geist, our tokens and clause colors. Cost: the generator writes each counter label once and swaps only the value, and the words "Key idea", "Step n", Added, Removed and Changed come from the stylesheet, so a figure grows by about 1.5 KB of markup, 0.37 KB gzipped on average (0.46 KB at most), and the shared CSS is about 3 KB (about 1 KB gzipped). Amends D28 (lessons: no effects).

nodes.choice: Learners write and run SQL inside the lesson page, with nothing to set up (owner decision, 2026-11-18, amended the same day): the `<RunSQL query={`…`} />` component (§6) turns a "Try it" query or an exercise starter into two separate boxes: the editor (a CodeMirror 6 editor with SQL colors, Run, Tables, an optional Auto-run switch, Reset query and Reset data) and the output ("n rows × m columns · time" and the result table, which scrolls inside its own box). Amends D4, D31, D41 and §15.
nodes.text: In-page SQL runner Learners write and run SQL inside the lesson page, with nothing to set up (owner decision, 2026-11-18, amended the same day): the `<RunSQL query={`…`} />` component (§6) turns a "Try it" query or an exercise starter into two separate boxes: the editor (a CodeMirror 6 editor with SQL colors, Run, Tables, an optional Auto-run switch, Reset query and Reset data) and the output ("n rows × m columns · time" and the result table, which scrolls inside its own box). The boxes sit side by side where the block is at least 36 rem wide (the lesson column plus up to 5 rem on each side of wide screens) and stack on phones; box 2 always shows an empty state ("Your result appears here…") before the first run. Amends D4, D31, D41 and §15. Learners should not leave the page for Colab or another tab, and should never notice the setup: they open the lesson and write queries, as on Hacker…
nodes.consequence: Learners should not leave the page for Colab or another tab, and should never notice the setup: they open the lesson and write queries, as on HackerRank or Programiz. Loading is invisible. DuckDB-Wasm (`@duckdb/duckdb-wasm`, exact version pinned in `package.json`, the `eh` bundle) is self-hosted in `dist/_astro` (no CDN, no third-party request before consent, §11). A lesson page ships one small deferred script (`src/scripts/run-sql.ts`, about 0.8 KB gzipped) that fetches nothing. After the load event, at idle (`requestIdleCallback`), once a block is within one screen of the viewport (`IntersectionObserver`), it loads in the background the controller (`sql-block.ts`, about 4 KB gzipped), the editor (CodeMirror, `sql-editor.ts`, about 120 KB gzipped), and the engine with the five cafe-sales CSVs from `datasets/cafe-sales/v1/` (`sql-runtime.ts` about 46 KB, the worker about 189 KB, the Wasm engine about 7.7 MB gzipped because GitHub Pages compresses `.wasm` with gzip, the CSVs about 35 KB). The engine compiles in a worker, so the page stays responsive. A visitor who only reads a lesson and never nears a block downloads about 3 KB for the runner (the script and 2 KB of CSS); one who scrolls near a block downloads about 8.1 MB once, then the browser cache serves it. Exception: with Data Saver (`navigator.connection.saveData`) or a 2G connection nothing is preloaded; loading starts on the first focus or Run. The UI uses no technical words about loading: if Run is pressed before the preparation has finished, box 2 shows "Getting ready…" with a thin progress bar and, once per page and never stored, "The first run takes a few seconds to get ready. After that, every run is instant." (a polite live region); the query then runs automatically. A loading failure says "Couldn't start. Check your connection and press Run again." Bundles: `eh` (34.2 MB raw, 7.7 MB gzip) is smaller than `mvp` (39.4 MB, 8.7 MB), and `coi` needs cross-origin isolation headers that GitHub Pages cannot send, so `eh` stays (it needs WebAssembly exception handling, present in every current browser); all 222 lesson queries (26 `<RunSQL>` plus 196 fenced) give identical results on `eh` and `mvp`. The stable release stays (owner-approved default). Tables panel: a Tables button lists the five tables with their columns, types and row counts, built at build time from `cafe-sales.sql` (`src/lib/cafe-schema.ts`), so it shows before anything loads; a table name adds `SELECT * FROM <table> LIMIT 10;` to the editor and Preview shows its first 5 rows. Errors show the first line of the engine's message without its jargon label plus a short tip for the common beginner mistakes (a missing or misspelled column, text without single quotes, a missing comma, an unclosed quote, a missing GROUP BY, an ambiguous column, SUM of text); each tip was tested against the engine (`src/scripts/sql-errors.ts`, `tests/sql-errors.test.ts`). Auto-run (off by default) re-runs a query that only reads data 800 ms after typing stops, only when the engine is already loaded, and shows errors quietly. Keyboard: Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs; Tab indents and Escape then Tab leaves the editor; focus is visible; light and dark follow the site theme. Playground: `/sql/playground/` (§3.1) is the same runner on a full-height page: editor and output side by side (stacked on phones), Tables as a side drawer, a friendly first query, five example queries that replace the editor text on click, Reset data and Reset query; without JavaScript it says it needs JavaScript and lists the examples. One database per page: every block shares it, so a table or view made in one block is seen by the next; Reset data drops everything and reloads the five tables. The result caps at 50 rows with a "n more rows" note. Nothing is stored (no `localStorage`, cookies or IndexedDB) and nothing is sent anywhere. Without JavaScript a lesson block is the plain highlighted code with a note. The engine is DuckDB 1.4.3 (Wasm build `1.32.0`); the lessons are checked against DuckDB 2.0.0 and 217 of 219 lesson queries give identical results (the two differences are unordered `INTERSECT` rows). A blank starter is fine for open exercises (owner-approved default), and rolling `<RunSQL>` out to all 35 lessons waits for the interleaved rewrite. The Colab button was dropped from the SQL stage by D43. Planned next, not part of this decision: Correct / Wrong self-checking on exercises (needs its own decision). Python and Excel are not affected.

nodes.consequence: A cheatsheet is a normal docs page (a page in `src/pages/`, not a lesson, so `classify()` ignores it) with an "On this page" list, in the sidebar after the stage's lessons and linked from the stage on `/start/` (`CHEATSHEETS` in `src/lib/roadmap.ts`). Its content is data (`src/data/cheatsheets/{stage}.ts`, shape in `src/lib/cheatsheet.ts`) drawn by one reusable component (`src/components/cheatsheet/Cheatsheet.astro`), so Excel and Python can reuse it. The Excel cheatsheet (`/excel/cheatsheet/`, "Excel in a nutshell") is data-first: its parts follow the flow of the data (shape, clean, query and summarize, combine tables, repeatable processing and quality, communicate), and each card ends with a "Next" line naming its twin in the coming stages (linked SQL lessons, pandas method names only); owner request 2026-11-19. Content comes only from published lessons of the stage (their big idea, Common trap and Check yourself), in the lessons' own cafe-sales vocabulary; each entry is a short pattern, one plain sentence, the most common trap where the lesson names one, and a link to its lesson. The Python cheatsheet (`/python/cheatsheet/`, "Python in a nutshell") exists (owner request, 2026-11-20): 27 cards, one for each of the lessons P1 to P27, in seven parts that follow the flow of the data (Python basics P1–P8; load and look P9–P11; select, derive, group, merge P12–P15; clean: missing, dates, text P16–P18; reshape and window-like columns P19–P20; charts and outside data P21–P23; ship it P24–P27), with three drawings of our own (split-apply-combine, a merge with `validate` and `indicator`, wide and long). Each card has its pattern in the lesson's own cafe-sales names, one plain sentence and the Common trap of its lesson; where a pandas pattern has a twin taught earlier, a short "Twin" line names it (linked SQL and Excel lessons, published ones only). Every pattern must run on the cafe-sales data (`scripts/check-cheatsheet-python.py`, wired as `npm run check:cheatsheet-python` and a step of `npm run check`; it needs pandas, numpy, openpyxl, matplotlib and seaborn and skips with a message when they are missing); its `$` lines are shell commands, checked only for existing. Lessons P1–P27 show the footer line "Sum it up: this lesson in the Python cheatsheet →" (card anchors `#p1` to `#p27`). SQL follows the three parts of D40 (S1–S17, S18–S30, S31–S35) and carries three small build-time inline SVG drawings of our own (clause order, join types, aggregate against window) in the clause colors of D41. Every SQL pattern must parse and run in DuckDB on the cafe-sales tables (`scripts/check-cheatsheet-sql.py`); `tests/cheatsheet.test.ts` checks that every cited lesson is published and inside its part. Card anchors are part of the URL contract, like reference pages (owner decision, 2026-11-19): a card's id is its lesson code in lowercase (`/sql/cheatsheet/#s8`, `/excel/cheatsheet/#e15`); when several cards share a lesson (Excel E4, E13) the first card on the page carries the id; an anchor is never renamed or reused without a redirect-style note in the changelog. Every published lesson that has a card shows one line in its footer next to "Unlocks next", "Sum it up: this lesson in the SQL cheatsheet →" (Excel likewise), built at build time from the sheet data (`cheatsheetLink` in `src/data/cheatsheets/index.ts`) so it cannot drift; lessons without a card show none; the Python stage has one too (below). The target card gets a calm `:target` outline and a `scroll-margin-top`; no JavaScript. Zero JavaScript of its own (the page ships only what every docs page ships, D31) and readable without JavaScript. One column on phones, a card grid on wide screens; print is one A4 sheet, both sides (two pages), black on white, no site chrome. The math block amends the note "linear algebra and calculus are not taught" in `research/curriculum/07-curriculum-rationale.md` (calculus is still not taught); when the two tracks are built, record the lessons in the curriculum map and SPEC §14.

nodes.consequence: The draft stage (25 lessons) was checked against five Python-for-data syllabi and changed as follows. Cut: `comprehensions` as a standalone lesson, folded into `lists-and-loops` (one-line list form only). Renamed and extended: `files-csv-json` becomes `files-and-tables` (adds `read_excel`, one `read_sql` query, the encoding rules and one DuckDB demo that reuses the SQL stage). Split: `charts` becomes `charts-matplotlib` (keeps the id `python-charts`, which other stages cite) and `charts-seaborn`. Added: `pandas-derived-columns` (`assign`, `map`, `apply`) and the exit capstone `cafe-quarterly-pack`, before `notebook-to-script`. Two awareness boxes, not lessons: Polars at the end of the stage and Plotly closing `charts-seaborn`. `environments-and-pip` is a required late lesson, no longer a stretch lesson. The twelve SQL-to-pandas bridge traps and the ten beginner traps of the issue each appear as a named exercise slot with a known-answer check, in the lesson the issue assigns (the traps the issue leaves open went to the obvious lesson, listed in the PR). Notebooks live in the repository, one per lesson, at `notebooks/python/{lesson-id}.ipynb` (named by lesson id, not slug), open through the Colab GitHub URL (§7) and read the cafe-sales tables from the `v0.1.0` tag (D39); the Google Drive folder named in the issue is not used. `reviewed` stays a date and every lesson stays `status: draft`. Lessons follow the interleaved shape of `LESSON-STANDARD.md`, with the known-answer slots inside Learn by doing. NumPy linear algebra is not taught in this stage and does not go to the advanced core, whatever §4 of the issue says: it belongs to the math block of the Data Scientist and ML Engineer tracks (D44), and `numpy-vectorization` shows one `@` example and points forward. Amends D32 and D40: 166 lessons in 8 stages (Excel 22, SQL 35, Python 27, core 25, Data Analyst 13, Data Engineer 20, Data Scientist 12, ML Engineer 12); `v1.0.0` is the four core stages (109 lessons). nodes.label: Advanced core shape
nodes.choice: 43 lessons in six parts of about four hours each, with one project that grows part by part, then one capstone case (44 lessons) (owner decisions, 2026-11-20, from research issues #71, #72, #73, #88, #89 and #92)
nodes.text: Advanced core shape 43 lessons in six parts of about four hours each, with one project that grows part by part, then one capstone case (44 lessons) (owner decisions, 2026-11-20, from research issues #71, #72, #73, #88, #89 and #92) Each part leans on what the learner already knows, familiar first, opens with a skip check (4 to 6 questions in `<details>`, no JavaScript; all right means go to the next part) and ends with a project step on cafe-sales; there is no separate capstone. 1 Statistics I (orders 10 to 70, Colab and pandas): descriptive report. 2 Statistics II and decisions (80 to 150): decision memo; `telling-the-story` also teaches chart choice, decluttering and takeaway titles for every role (owner question, 2026-11-20; visualization defines the Data Analyst in #87), while interactive charts and BI dashboards stay in the Data Analyst track and model plots in the Data Scientist a…
nodes.consequence: Each part leans on what the learner already knows, familiar first, opens with a skip check (4 to 6 questions in `<details>`, no JavaScript; all right means go to the next part) and ends with a project step on cafe-sales; there is no separate capstone. 1 Statistics I (orders 10 to 70, Colab and pandas): descriptive report. 2 Statistics II and decisions (80 to 150): decision memo; `telling-the-story` also teaches chart choice, decluttering and takeaway titles for every role (owner question, 2026-11-20; visualization defines the Data Analyst in #87), while interactive charts and BI dashboards stay in the Data Analyst track and model plots in the Data Scientist and ML Engineer tracks. 3 Shapes of data (160 to 210): new `modeling-the-domain` (entities, relationships, reading an entity-relationship diagram, many-to-many as a table, grain declared before DDL; use depth for all roles, #89 finding 1), grain and facts, star schema, ML framing, leakage, error-cost metrics; project step: a star schema. 4 Engineering on your laptop (220 to 290, D48): `laptop-setup-and-terminal`, Git (saving a history), `python-project-layout`, `environments-and-dependencies` (uv), `debugging-and-retries`, `testing-with-pytest`, `logging-config-secrets`, `readable-code-and-classes` (type hints, docstrings, ruff, reading docs, library classes and one `@dataclass`; inheritance recognized only); project step: a tested repository. 5 Teamwork, scale and the platform (300 to 350): Git branches, pull requests and review, `data-beyond-tables` (nested JSON, events, the two format pairs, flatten, explode, normalize), `a-feel-for-scale` (dict and set cost at use depth, no formal Big-O), cloud (the eight infrastructure concepts of #72, access control and governance), new `inside-the-database` (query plans as operator trees, why the planner skips an index, what a transaction promises and why numbers move during a refresh, replica versus backup, stored procedures and triggers recognized; recognition depth, #89 finding 2), warehouses and cost (adds additive versus non-additive measures); project step: a reviewed pull request, Parquet, the star schema loaded into DuckDB with one plan read and one cost estimate. 6 Working with AI (360 to 430, about four hours; owner request to put it last before the tracks, #88): `what-ai-can-and-cannot-do` (the capability map as a cliff: tidy tasks near the ceiling, realistic ones far below, every number dated), `prompting-with-the-data-in-the-room` (the context pack as a standing file), `trust-but-verify-ai-output` (45 minutes; every AI task ends in accept, revise or reject), `find-the-planted-error` (errors named first) and `hunt-the-unflagged-error`, `ai-statistics-and-stories` (wrong test choice, p-hacking, causal verbs, citations that do not resolve), `what-stays-human`, RAG and agents; project step: one AI-assisted analysis with its context pack and a verification log, the README and the final memo, then the capstone. Capstone (order 440, about 4 hours, owner request 2026-11-20): `capstone-two-quiet-weeks`, a real openly licensed dataset (UCI Bike Sharing, Capital Bikeshare 2011–2012, CC BY 4.0, downloaded from UCI, not hosted) with our own brief; no politics (owner); any of Excel, SQL or Python; an open answer graded by a rubric on the chain of reasoning; AI use allowed and documented in a verification log; the reference answer, in `<details>`, ends with a section that says the author knew the learner would use AI and names the shortcuts AI takes on this data (research #92 design rules); then `/choose-your-track/` (D50). The thesis of the part is that the fundamentals are the detectors of AI mistakes. Capability numbers live in one dated box per lesson, reviewed every six months; the rest of the part is reviewed yearly. No separate ethics lesson: consent and personal data (PII) go into C1, access control and governance into the cloud lesson, and personal data in prompts into the AI lessons. Docker is an awareness box in the cloud lesson; build depth is in the DE and ML tracks, as are CI/CD, inheritance authorship and validation libraries (pandera, pydantic). Database internals (#89): relational algebra and calculus are skipped (the operators are taught as the boxes of a query plan); the Data Engineer track gets a ten-lesson database internals module (orders 200 to 290: plans and operators, indexes, join algorithms, row and column storage, transactions and isolation, write skew, locks and MVCC, WAL and recovery, architectures and trade-offs, procedures and triggers), each shown by a real run on free tools except recovery internals; data mining belongs to the Data Scientist track. Building agents, RAG pipelines and evaluation harnesses belongs to the ML Engineer and Data Engineer tracks. The DSA practice gym of #73 is planned after the tracks exist and is not built. Ids and slugs of existing lessons are unchanged and `order` is renumbered in steps of 10 (core and tracks are unpublished, so no URL changes). Counts: core 44 (43 plus the capstone), curriculum 195 lessons in 8 stages (Excel 22, SQL 35, Python 27, core 44, Data Analyst 13, Data Engineer 30, Data Scientist 12, ML Engineer 12); `v1.0.0` is the four core stages (128 lessons). Worked examples of the statistics lessons keep their `app-events` or `cafe-sales` dataset; project steps use cafe-sales. Part sizes (sum of lesson minutes, before skip check and project step): 185, 240, 170, 245, 165 and 240. Showing the six parts on `/start/` needs a `part` field in the lesson schema (§5, a CONTRACT change) and is left as a TODO. Amends D32, D40, D45 and D48.

nodes.label: The logo
nodes.text: The logo

nodes.label: Concept
nodes.text: Concept The database (SQL) is the core every data career passes through (Excel → SQL → Python → Data Analyst / Data Engineer / Data Scientist). Following Grok's principle — the black hole is never drawn, only the light around it — the database is not drawn as a shape; it is the void at the centre of a disc of light. The void is the "unknown" that data science and AI explore; the three traced layers make it read instantly as a database.

nodes.label: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`)
nodes.text: Construction (viewBox `0 0 100 100`) ```svg <svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"> <circle class="disc" cx="50" cy="50" r="46" fill="#f4f4f4"/> <path class="void" d="M29 31C29 17 71 17 71 31V69C71 83 29 83 29 69Z" fill="#000"/> <g class="bands" fill="none" stroke="#f4f4f4" stroke-width="4" stroke-linecap="round"> <path d="M29 31C29 45 71 45 71 31"/> <!-- top rim --> <path d="M29 45C29 59 71 59 71 45"/> <!-- layer 1 --> <path d="M29 59C29 73 71 73 71 59"/> <!-- layer 2 --> </g> </svg> ``` Keep the class names (`disc`, `void`, `bands`) — the animation depends on them.

nodes.label: Usage rules
nodes.text: Usage rules - Default: white logo on black. Use `logo-light-bg.svg` only on light surfaces. - The void must always be the background colour (it is a hole, not a black shape). On a non-black background, use the inline version and set `--logo-bg` to that background. - Minimum size 16 px. Clear space around it = ¼ of its width. - No outlines, glows, gradients, rotation or added elements (stars, sparkles were tried and removed on purpose). - Wordmark: datafromzero, lowercase, Geist 500, letter-spacing −0.01em, to the right of the mark; tagline *From A1 to AI* in Geist Mono when space allows. ---

nodes.label: Logo animation (approved — match `logo-animation.mp4`)
nodes.text: Logo animation (approved — match `logo-animation.mp4`) Total ≈ 2.9 s. All in `logo/logo-animation.js`. | # | What happens | Duration / ease | |---|---|---| | 1 | A thin 1.2 px ring of light traces the circle, starting at 12 o'clock, clockwise | 1.1 s, `power2.inOut` | | 2 | The disc scales up from the centre and fills in; the trace fades out | 1.0 s, `expo.out` (overlap −0.15 s) | | 3 | The void (database) opens from the centre (scaleY 0→1, scaleX .7→1) | 1.0 s, `expo.out` (overlap −0.7 s) | | 4 | The three layer lines draw left→right, staggered | 0.6 s each, stagger .12, `power2.out` | - Plays once on homepage load, as CSS keyframes (first paint never waits for GSAP). Tap/click the logo to replay: the replay re-runs the whole hero lockup (logo and wordmark, §5) and the selection box with it. - On the homepage the logo is part of the lockup with the wordmark "From A1 to AI." (§5); the wordmark's own motion follows the logo: words rise from 0.9 s, the selection box lands on "A1" at 1.5 s, and the reel rolls 1 → I from 2.2 s for 1.1 s (`power3.inOut`). The intro ends at about 3.3 s. - `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` → no animation, logo shown static. - Nav logo: static, never animated. ---

nodes.label: 5a. Bottom taskbar (every page, SPEC D31, D35)
nodes.text: 5a. Bottom taskbar (every page, SPEC D31, D35) Approved mockup (owner, 2026-11), built as `src/components/taskbar/Taskbar.astro`: a floating, rounded glass bar (16px radius, blur 16px, max-width 720px, centered on the content column, 16px from the bottom plus the safe-area inset) on the homepage, project pages, lessons and reference, phone and desktop. Mobile navigation is one bar (D35): Starlight's header menu button and "On this page" bar are hidden on phones. - Left: the menu button, a menu icon (two bars that cross into ×) and a two-line label: a small mono line (Geist Mono 500, 11px, muted) and the page title (Geist 500, 15px), both with an ellipsis. On a lesson the small line is `E8 · current section` and follows the scroll (the page's h2s); on the homepage it is the section on screen (Home · The core · Careers · Three tools · History · Directions) over the site name; elsewhere it is the current h2 or empty. - Right: a solid primary button: "Next E9 →" on a lesson (next published lesson in the stage, else the next stage's first, else "Roadmap" to `/start/`), "Start E1 →" (the first published lesson) on `/start/`, "Start here →" to `/start/` everywhere else. Back to top (a chevron, dimmed in the first 200px) shows at every width; the light / dark switch moved into the sheet. nodes.label: Build notes for Astro Starlight
nodes.text: Build notes for Astro Starlight Priorities (in order): stability & speed → mobile-first (most readers are on phones) → nice motion. - Where GSAP is allowed: the homepage only (SPEC D28). Project pages, stories, lessons, exercises and reference pages load no motion script — they stay plain Starlight for speed, plus the taskbar's one small script (§5a, SPEC D31: under 1 KB gzipped, CSS transitions only). - Homepage: build it as a custom Astro page (its own layout, not the docs layout), port the prototype into components, and load GSAP only there (`<script>` inside the page/component so it is bundled per-page). - GSAP: `npm i gsap` (3.13+; all plugins are free now). Any plugin, each effect loaded on demand (SPEC D28). Use `gsap.matchMedia()` for reduced-motion and pointer checks, and kill ScrollTriggers on page leave if client-side navigation is enabled. - Starlight config: use `logo/logo-dark-bg.svg` as the site logo (with a light-theme variant `logo-light-bg.svg` if light mode is kept) and `logo/favicon.svg` as the favicon. Site name = placeholder. - Docs area look: apply the tokens in §2 (black background, Geist / Geist Mono) through Starlight's custom CSS so lessons and reference match the homepage. Two modes: - Study / lessons: open, quiet, one idea per screen, generous spacing. - Reference: book-like, indexed, searchable (Starlight's built-in search), compact. - Math: DS / Statistics pages need LaTeX — add `remark-math` + `rehype-katex` (and KaTeX CSS). - Fonts: self-host or use Google Fonts with `display=swap`; preload Geist 400 and, on the homepage, Geist 500 (the hero wordmark). - Performance budget: JS before first paint ≈ 3 KB gzipped, effects loaded on demand (SPEC D28); no images required — everything is SVG/CSS. Content must be fully readable with JS disabled (GSAP sets hidden states, CSS never hides content by default — the prototype already works this way). ---

nodes.label: 1. The project this package serves
nodes.text: 1. The project this package serves Data From Zero is a free, visual-first learning site that teaches its own original content. The path shape is already decided and is not reopened by this research: - One linear path: Excel → SQL (one complete block) → Python → advanced core → five career tracks. - The five tracks: Data Analyst, Data Engineer, Data Scientist, Analytics Engineer, ML/AI Engineer. - Free in full. No paywall, no account wall for reading and learning, no free-tier funnel. The whole path is the product. - Visual-first teaching. Each core concept gets a canonical visual or interactive demonstration, not just prose and code. - Bilingual-ready by structure: English at the root, Vietnamese under `/vi/`. The Vietnamese edition is scaffolding — terminology, examples, and format guidance built for Vietnamese learners — not a machine translation of the English pages. - Repo as source of truth. Site content lives as Markdown in the repository; a sync step mirrors it into the website. A published page's URL does not change; a rename requires a redirect. Later owner decision (2026-11-17, SPEC D32): the site has four career tracks. Analytics Engineer is no longer a track; its skills live in Data Engineer and Data Analyst. The research below predates that decision and is kept as written. Judge every recommendation in this package against four tests from the project charter: does it beat the incumbents on clarity, on visual and intuitive teaching, on time-to-skill, and on caree…

nodes.label: Canonical source rule
nodes.text: Canonical source rule Wave 4 produced a dedupe map so the package does not carry two competing versions of the same topic. When files overlap, one file is canonical: - Topic lists in `02` come only from the syllabus inventory files. Other waves contribute overlays, not second lists. - The interview layer (patterns, ladders, take-home design) is owned by the Wave 2 interview research. - The lesson template is owned by the Wave 3 lesson-anatomy research. - Visual techniques are owned by the Wave 3 visual-teaching research. - Site-level patterns and platform scores are owned by the Wave 1 UI/UX audit. - What certifications test is owned by the Wave 2 certification map. - All `/vi/` rules — terminology, glossary, format traps, scaffolding — are owned by the Wave 3 Vietnamese-learners research. If a draft contradicts the canonical file on its own topic, the canonical file wins and the draft is fixed. ---

nodes.label: 01 — Competitor map → positioning and scope guardrails
nodes.text: 01 — Competitor map → positioning and scope guardrails Use it to decide what Data From Zero must match to be credible (sequencing transparency, project cadence, honest time math) and where it wins by structure rather than by volume (free in full, visual teaching, Vietnamese scaffolding, one committed order). It also records what not to chase: matching a catalog count, minting a competing credential, or rebuilding a company-tagged interview bank.

nodes.label: 02 — Syllabus inventory → the lesson backlog
nodes.text: 02 — Syllabus inventory → the lesson backlog Use it as the checklist for coverage. Each domain section is the topic backlog for that stage of the path, with hiring and certification overlays showing which topics are tested first and hardest. Build order follows the linear path; within a domain, build order follows the inventory order unless the teaching playbook gives a pedagogical reason to resequence. Two explicit scope decisions are recorded here so they are not misread as oversights: - Algorithm inventory scope. There is no dedicated algorithm inventory in this package at the same completeness standard as the SQL, Python, and Excel inventories. Algorithmic material exists in three places only: ML algorithm families inside the ML inventory, a data-structures-and-algorithms block described in the OSSU supplement, and coding-round patterns in the interview layer. Package `02` states that scope plainly. Do not present the package as containing a full algorithms curriculum, and do not let a syllabus page imply one exists. If the ML/AI track later needs complexity intuition, sorting and searching, and common interview algorithm patterns as first-class topics, that inventory must be commissioned separately. - Mathematics foundations note. Statistics is inventoried in depth. Linear algebra and calculus for ML are not inventoried as a main-path block; they appear as sequencing choices in the WQU and OSSU supplements and as assumed background in the ML inventory. The ML/AI track p…

nodes.label: 03 — Teaching playbook → lesson production standard
nodes.text: 03 — Teaching playbook → lesson production standard Use it as the production template: the timed lesson anatomy, the worked-example-to-independent-problem progression, the five-rung exercise ladder per domain, and the checkpoint tiers with failure diagnosis and spaced review. Thresholds in the underlying research that are marked [Recommendation] are design choices for Data From Zero, not research findings. They keep that label in the package. Do not quote them elsewhere as evidence. The playbook also carries a short note on checkpoint integrity in an era of AI-generated answers: checkpoints are designed around blank-start work and narration of choices, so a copied answer is visible as a gap in reasoning rather than as a pass.

nodes.label: 04 — UI/UX lessons → site build
nodes.text: 04 — UI/UX lessons → site build Use it for the two-space design (Learn as a spacious study layout; Reference as a dense book layout), for path-card and lesson-page anatomy, and for the friction rules: full syllabus visible before commitment, no hidden pricing because there is no price, progress shown as checkmarks on a map rather than as streak pressure. Visual-technique build costs and the top visual assets to build first are in `03` and `04` together — `03` owns the concept techniques, `04` owns the site patterns that present them.

nodes.label: 05 — Career and viral → endings and distribution
nodes.text: 05 — Career and viral → endings and distribution Use it for how each stage and each track ends: the job tasks learners must be able to do, the portfolio artifacts they must be able to show, and the external proof points worth naming (for example, free third-party certificates and drill plans) without pretending Data From Zero issues them. Boundary — read this before using `05`. The career file covers *what to learn and prove*: hiring-task taxonomies, portfolio standards per track, and credential alignment. It does not cover resume writing, LinkedIn presentation, or application workflow end to end. No file in this package does. Do not scope `05`, or any page built from it, as full job-search coaching. If that layer is wanted later, it needs its own research and its own file. The viral half of `05` covers audience, positioning moves, and shareability mechanics (the map as the shareable artifact, the open license, the public challenge pattern). It is distribution design, not a marketing plan with dates and budgets. ---

nodes.label: Honesty rules for anyone quoting this package (binding)
nodes.text: Honesty rules for anyone quoting this package (binding) These rules come directly from the Wave 4 strike and flag list. They govern the package files themselves and any site copy, deck, or post built from them. 1. Never present a self-contradictory vendor total as one number. DataCamp's own pages give different track and catalog hour totals in different places; Coursera's own pages give different course counts and hour totals for the same program (see `01` for the Google Data Analytics and IBM cases). When a vendor contradicts itself, show the versions with their sources, or pick one version and name it. Never average them, never pick the largest, and never cite a blended figure as if a single page stated it. 2. DataCamp price — one dated formulation only. Write: list price about $28 per month billed annually; the pricing page simultaneously promotes an $11 per month special price. Date the observation (checked 2026-11-15). Do not publish either figure alone as "the price," because the page shows both at once and promotions rotate. 3. IBM program counts — versioned, never blended. IBM Data Analyst: 11 courses in the current V3 version (older issued badges show 9), about 151 learning hours. IBM Data Engineering: state the course count and the hour figure as two separately sourced facts with their versions; do not present "16 courses / 217 hours" as a single-source fact, because the hour figure in the badge text attaches to the earlier course set. 4. Job-demand rankings — #1-o…

nodes.label: How the research was done
nodes.text: How the research was done - Wave 1 mapped 13 platform and syllabus areas. Wave 2 added the interview and job-task layer, projects and portfolio expectations, the AI-era layer, a certification map, and two supplements (WorldQuant University and OSSU) added by the Owner on 2026-11-15. Wave 3 distilled lesson design, visual teaching, and Vietnamese-learner specifics. Wave 4 verified and deduped. - Wave 4 checked 30 highest-risk claims across Waves 1 and 2 claim by claim against live official pages, plus 12 Wave 3 claims and a full cross-wave dedupe. Result across the two main verification passes: 19 confirmed, 7 partially confirmed, 2 unverified, 2 contradicted — and both contradicted items were inconsistencies inside the sources themselves, not errors introduced by the research files. The Wave 3 pass found no contradicted claims. Headline finding: no invented numbers were found anywhere in the corpus. Every failure was framing, sample-blending, or versioning, and each is fixed by the rules below. - Confidence is marked per section in the source files. In this package, a claim carried without a caveat has either been confirmed in Wave 4 or rests on a directly opened primary page in its own wave. Claims that remain second-hand, sample-specific, or design judgment are labeled as such where they appear.

nodes.label: What remains unverified or out of scope
nodes.text: What remains unverified or out of scope - CLF-C02 price and duration: unverified from an official page; omitted by design. - One Wave 3 claim about Khan Academy unit gating was not independently re-opened in Wave 4; it is cited in the package with its Wave 3 attribution, not as a Wave 4-verified fact. - Discussion and community evidence in the positioning research is paraphrased pattern-level material gathered via search excerpts and aggregating articles; it is not population statistics and is not presented as such. - Google Trends comparisons could not be retrieved in the research session; demand arguments rest on job-posting analyses and surveys instead, with samples named. ---

nodes.label: 5. How to work with this package
nodes.text: 5. How to work with this package 1. Start from the decision, not the file. Positioning question → `01`. Coverage question → `02`. "How do I build this lesson?" → `03`. "How does the site present it?" → `04`. "What must the learner be able to prove, and how does this spread?" → `05`. 2. Respect the canonical rule in §2. If you need a topic list, take it from `02`. If you need a site pattern, take it from `04`'s audit lineage. Do not re-derive a second version inside a page draft. 3. Carry the honesty rules into site copy. Any number that reaches a public page — a comparison, a salary figure, a demand percentage, a star count — must satisfy §4 first. When in doubt, name the sample and the date, or drop the number. 4. Keep the boundaries visible. Pages built from `05` say "what to learn and prove" and link onward for resume and application help rather than implying coverage that does not exist. Pages touching algorithms state the inventory scope in §3 rather than implying a full algorithms track. 5. Treat the wave files as the audit trail. This package is the synthesis; the underlying wave files in the research folder hold the per-claim URLs, access dates, and confidence marks. Cite the package for decisions; consult the wave files when a specific number is challenged. ---
