nodes.label: Slug rules
nodes.text: Slug rules - Lowercase English, kebab-case, ASCII only: `/sql/window-functions/`. Vietnamese pages reuse the English slug. - No numbers, dates or versions in slugs. Order comes from `order` in frontmatter. - Always a trailing slash (`trailingSlash: 'always'`). - The slug is derived from the file name; the file name is the slug.

nodes.label: Change rules
nodes.text: Change rules - Never rename or delete a published URL. If a rename is unavoidable: 1. add an entry to `src/redirects.ts` (old → new), 2. keep the lesson `id` unchanged (§5.1), 3. note it in `CHANGELOG.md`. - A retired page stays online with `status: deprecated` and a link to its replacement. - Anchors (`#heading-id`) on reference pages are part of the contract — headings there are not renamed casually.

nodes.label: Linking inside content
nodes.text: Linking inside content - Internal links are root-relative (`/sql/joins/`), never absolute (`https://datafromzero.github.io/…`). - Link to other lessons by path; the build validates every internal link (§12). ---

nodes.label: Information architecture
nodes.text: Information architecture ``` datafromzero ├─ Learn (Study mode — open, quiet, one idea per screen) │ ├─ 1 Excel / Sheets → 2 SQL → 3 Python → 4 Advanced core │ └─ Branches: Data Analyst · Data Engineer · Data Scientist · ML/AI Engineer ├─ Reference (Book mode — indexed, compact, searchable) │ ├─ Glossary │ ├─ Syntax: Excel functions · SQL keywords · pandas │ ├─ Statistics formulas │ └─ Careers (4 guides) ├─ Stories (history, explainers, visualizations — motion allowed) ├─ Datasets └─ About · Cite · Changelog · License · Privacy ``` Sidebar order and grouping are generated from frontmatter (`stage`, `order`), never hand-maintained. ---

nodes.label: Content model
nodes.text: Content model Schemas are registered in `src/content.config.ts` and defined in `src/lib/content-schemas.ts`; validation runs on every build (`src/lib/content-validation.ts`). Adding an optional field = MINOR change. Adding a required field, renaming or removing a field = MAJOR change + migration script. Rules for every type (D17): - `id` is lowercase kebab-case (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`) and unique across all content types (an English page and its Vietnamese translation share one id). - The file's folder decides its type (paths in the headings below). A file nested deeper than its type allows fails the build. - Every id reference must point to an existing entry of the right type. - `sources[].url` and `sheet` must be `http(s)` URLs. - The build reports all problems at once, naming the file and field, and fails.

nodes.label: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Lesson (`src/content/docs/{stage}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: sql-joins # permanent internal key; never changes, even if the slug does title: Joining tables short_title: Joins # optional, ≤ 24 chars, one sidebar line; required when a published title is over 26 chars (D47) description: Combine rows from two tables with INNER and LEFT JOIN. # ≤ 160 chars, used for SEO/social stage: sql # excel | sql | python | core | data-analyst | data-engineer | # data-scientist | ml-engineer order: 40 # sort key inside the stage; use gaps of 10 so lessons can be inserted level: beginner # beginner | intermediate | advanced duration: 25 # minutes, integer objectives: # 2–5 items, each starts with a verb - Explain what a join key is - Write an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN prerequisites: # lesson ids (not URLs); validated at build time - sql-select-basics datasets: [cafe-sales] # dataset names (§7); optional notebook: notebooks/python/py-pandas-joins.ipynb # optional, Python stage on (D43); drives the "Open in Colab" button sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/…/copy # optional; Excel stage "Make a copy" link reviewed: 2026-11-15 # last date the content was checked for correctness sources: # at least 1; documentation, papers, books - title: PostgreSQL documentation — Joined tables url: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/queries-table-expressions.html status: published # draft | published | deprecated replaced_by: null # lesson id, required when status = deprecated --- ``` - `stage` must match the lesson's folder. - `status: draft` lessons are built only in local dev, never deployed (D18). A published or deprecated lesson may not list a draft in `prerequisites` or `replaced_by`. - A deprecated lesson shows a notice linking to `replaced_by` (§3.3). Rendered at the top of every lesson: code · level · duration · last reviewed (the code is the stage prefix plus `order / 10`, e.g. E8; a label, never part of a URL, D34), then Objectives and Before this lesson (prerequisite links). Rendered at the bottom: Unlocks next (the lessons that list this one in `prerequisites`, drafts excluded, in the reader's language, computed at build time without JavaScript; hidden when empty), Sources, Cite this lesson, Suggest an edit, Report an issue, prev/next. - Inside one stage, `order` must be a topological order of `prerequisites`: a prerequisite in the same stage has a smaller `order`. Prerequisite cycles fail the check (`scripts/check-graph.ts`, §12).

nodes.label: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Reference entry (`src/content/docs/reference/{area}/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: ref-sql-group-by title: GROUP BY area: sql # excel | sql | pandas | stats summary: Groups rows that share values so aggregates are computed per group. syntax: | # optional, shown in a code block at the top SELECT col, AGG(x) FROM t GROUP BY col; see_also: [ref-sql-having, glossary-aggregate] # ids used_in: [sql-aggregation] # lesson ids; optional (can also be computed) reviewed: 2026-11-15 sources: [ … ] --- ``` Reference pages use a fixed section order: Syntax → Parameters → Examples → Common mistakes → See also. `area` must match the folder. `see_also` is required (an empty list is allowed); its ids may be reference entries or glossary terms. `used_in` must name existing lessons that are not drafts (D18).

nodes.label: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`)
nodes.text: Glossary term (`src/content/docs/reference/glossary/{slug}.md`) ```yaml --- id: glossary-primary-key term: Primary key short: A column whose value uniquely identifies each row. # ≤ 140 chars, used in hover/inline tooltips aliases: [PK] # required; an empty list is allowed reviewed: 2026-11-15 --- ``` `term` is also used as the page title.

nodes.label: Career guide, Story, Dataset
nodes.text: Career guide, Story, Dataset - Career (`/careers/{career}/`): `id`, `title`, `summary`, `skills[]`, `stages[]` (which stages/branches to finish), `reviewed`, `sources[]`. - Story (`/stories/{slug}/`): `id`, `title`, `description`, `published`, `reviewed`, `sources[]`, `motion: true|false`. - Dataset (`/datasets/{name}/`): files are defined in §7. Page frontmatter is not defined yet (D19); until it is, the build rejects dataset pages other than `datasets/index`. ---

nodes.label: Authoring components
nodes.text: Authoring components The only components content may use. Each must degrade to readable static HTML without JS. | Component | Purpose | No-JS fallback | |---|---|---| | `<Exercise id="sql-joins-1">` … `</Exercise>` | Numbered exercise block | Plain block | | `<Solution>` … `</Solution>` (inside `Exercise`) | Hidden answer, "Show solution" | Native `<details>` | | `<OpenInColab />` | Button from the lesson's `notebook` field | Plain link | | `<OpenInSheets />` | "Make a copy" button from the lesson's `sheet` field | Plain link | | ``<RunSQL query={`SELECT …`} />`` | Two boxes (editor and output) with Run, Tables, Auto-run and resets against the cafe-sales tables (D42); the editor and engine load in the background near the block | The plain highlighted code block and a note | | `<Term id="glossary-primary-key">primary key</Term>` | Inline glossary link with short definition | Plain link | | Starlight `<Aside>` (note / tip / caution / danger) | Callouts | Built in | | `$…$`, `$$…$$` | Math (KaTeX) | MathML | Rules: - No other components or raw `<script>` in content. New components are added here first (MINOR change). - Components are available in every `.mdx` file without import lines (D21). The build fails, naming the file and line, on any `import`/`export` in content, any component not in this table, any `<script>`, event-handler attribute (`on…=`), `set:html` or `javascript:` URL (in `.md` or `.mdx`), a `Solution` outside an `Exercise`, or math inside a heading. - `Term` shows the definition as a native popover, with no JS: opened by hover/focus where interest invokers exist (`interestfor`), otherwise by a small "?" button next to the link (`popovertarget`, tap or click). Both dismiss with Esc or an outside click; the link always goes to the glossary page. - A literal dollar sign in prose must be written `\$`; otherwise `$…$` is read as math. - Step-by-step figures and concept animations (D41) are not components: the generator `scripts/make-animation.mjs` prints plain `<figure class="sa">` or `<figure class="ca">` markup (`<input>`s, an `<svg>`, `<label>` controls and an `<ol>` or a caption) that the lesson `.mdx` carries as raw HTML, styled by `src/styles/step-animation.css`. Lowercase HTML elements pass the content rules; no `<script>`, no `style` attribute, no new import. - `RunSQL` takes the starting SQL in a `query` template string (an empty one fails the build, naming the file); a blank starter is a comment such as `-- Write your query here`. It goes in place of the fenced block of a "Try it" query or an exercise starter; hints, half-solutions and solutions stay plain code blocks. - Exercise ids are permanent (`{lesson-id}-{n}`) so teachers can reference "Exercise sql-joins-2".

nodes.label: In-browser code
nodes.text: In-browser code Write runnable examples as fenced code blocks with a meta flag: ```` ```sql dataset=cafe-sales ````. SQL examples that learners should run use `<RunSQL>` (D42, above). Other fenced blocks stay plain code; a future Python runner (Pyodide) could pick them up without editing content. ---

nodes.label: Datasets
nodes.text: Datasets ``` datasets/ cafe-sales/ v1/ orders.csv customers.csv README.md # description, columns, types, row counts, how it was generated, license schema.yaml # machine-readable column definitions ``` - A small set of synthetic datasets the author creates, reused from Excel through Python so learners see the same data in every tool. No personal data. - Immutable once released. A change in columns or values = new folder `v2/`; `v1/` stays forever, so old notebooks and spreadsheets keep working. - Notebooks (Python stage on, D43) load data from a release-tag URL, not `main`: `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/v1.0.0/datasets/cafe-sales/v1/orders.csv` Until `v1.0.0` exists, notebooks use the pre-release tag `v0.1.0` (D39), for example `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/v0.1.0/datasets/cafe-sales/v1/cafe-sales.sql`. `v1/` never changes, so those links keep working after `v1.0.0`. - Each dataset also ships an `.xlsx` (Excel stage) and a `.sql` load script (SQL stage) generated by a script in `scripts/`. - License: CC BY 4.0. A companion dataset (D46) is a second folder in `datasets/` with the same layout (`v1/`, `README.md`, `schema.yaml`, a generator in `scripts/`, CC BY 4.0) whose rows refer to a main dataset by key. `cafe-menu-accents` refers to cafe-sales by `store_id` and `product_id` and ships only a CSV, because only the Python stage uses it. Adding a companion never changes a released `v1/` folder of the main dataset. Notebooks (none in the SQL stage, D43; Colab is introduced in the Python stage): `notebooks/{stage}/{lesson-id}.ipynb`, opened via `https://colab.research.google.com/github/datafromzero/datafromzero.github.io/blob/main/notebooks/…`. Notebooks are cleared of outputs before commit (CI check). ---

nodes.label: Internationalization
nodes.text: Internationalization > Paused (D30). The site is English only until the owner reactivates this section. Nothing below is > built meanwhile: no `vi` locale, and any page under `src/content/docs/vi/` fails the build. The rules stay > as written for when Vietnamese returns (set `VI_ENABLED` in `src/site.ts`, remove the `/vi/` redirects). - Starlight i18n with `root` locale English and `vi` locale. UI strings translated in `src/content/i18n/vi.json`. - Vietnamese files mirror English paths: `src/content/docs/vi/sql/joins.md` with the same `id`. - Untranslated pages fall back to English with Starlight's "not yet translated" notice. - A translation records `translated_from_version` (curriculum version it was translated from) so stale translations can be listed. It is required on every Vietnamese page of a typed collection (§5), and the page must have an English counterpart at the mirrored path with the same `id`. - Code, SQL keywords and dataset column names stay in English in both languages. ---

nodes.label: Versioning, citation, changelog
nodes.text: Versioning, citation, changelog - Curriculum version (SemVer), tagged on GitHub as `vX.Y.Z`: - MAJOR — curriculum restructure, a required schema change, or any URL redirect batch - MINOR — new lessons, reference entries, datasets, components, optional fields - PATCH — corrections, clarifications, link fixes - Each GitHub Release is archived by Zenodo (GitHub integration) → one concept DOI (always latest) + one DOI per version. - `CITATION.cff` at repo root (title, author, version, date, concept DOI, license). Updated on every release. - `/cite/` page: APA + BibTeX for the whole work, generated at build time from `CITATION.cff` (the build fails if its `version` differs from `package.json`); the DOI line reads "after the first release" until Zenodo exists, then shows the concept DOI and per-version DOIs. - Every lesson footer shows Cite this lesson: author, year (from `reviewed`), title, site, curriculum version, URL. Static pages cannot know when they were read, so a note asks the reader to add their access date (D20). - `CHANGELOG.md` follows *Keep a Changelog*; `/changelog/` renders it (single source, no copy); `/license/` shows `LICENSE` and `LICENSE-CONTENT` the same way. - The site footer shows the current version and its DOI badge. ---

nodes.label: content-producer
nodes.text: Writes lessons - draft lesson text when the owner asks for team drafts (D24), or the material around the owner's own text - with exercises and solutions, practice workbooks (Excel), notebooks (SQL, Python), datasets, sources and frontmatter. Use for content production (build plan item 8), one batch of up to five lessons per agent, in a worktree when batches run in parallel.

nodes.label: content-reviewer
nodes.text: Fact-checks a finished batch of lessons before it goes to the owner - recomputes the numbers from the dataset, checks formulas, queries and code give the stated results, checks tool claims against official docs, and checks the lesson standard. Read-only. Use once per lesson batch, after the writer reports a green `npm run check`.

nodes.label: maintainer
nodes.text: Routine upkeep - verifies Dependabot/dependency bumps build cleanly, fixes typos and small wording or link errors, drafts issue triage, lists lessons whose `reviewed` date is older than 18 months (SPEC §12). Use for small, low-risk, well-defined chores; escalates anything else.

nodes.label: qa-runner
nodes.text: Runs the build and quality gates (npm ci, npm run build, npm run check, link check, Lighthouse) and reports only failures. Read-only - never edits. Use after every implementation step, before spec-reviewer, and for routine health checks.

nodes.label: site-builder
nodes.text: Implements site code and visuals - Astro/Starlight config, content collections and Zod schemas, authoring components, scripts, CI and quality gates, project pages, design tokens, theme, homepage motion with GSAP, accessibility and Lighthouse fixes, bug fixes. Use for any code or visual change bigger than a few lines.

nodes.label: spec-reviewer
nodes.text: Reviews site code, config, schema, URL, dataset and SPEC changes against SPEC.md CONTRACT sections, CLAUDE.md hard rules and the design handoff before merge. Also consulted before any change to a CONTRACT or a SPEC §1 decision. Read-only. Not for routine lesson batches (content-reviewer does those). Use once per code PR, after a green build.

nodes.label: vi-translator
nodes.text: PAUSED (D30, English only) - do not use until the owner reactivates SPEC §8. Translates English pages and UI strings into Vietnamese under src/content/docs/vi/ and src/content/i18n/vi.json, and lists stale translations. Use when English pages are ready to mirror, or to refresh translations after an English page changes.

nodes.label: astro.config.mjs
nodes.text: @ts-check https://astro.build/config Fonts stay separate files: inlined as base64 they bloated the render-blocking stylesheet (rarely used subsets included) and could not be cached or skipped via unicode-range. SPEC §3.2: every URL ends with a trailing slash. SPEC §3.3: renamed URLs keep working through redirects. SPEC D27: Astro's JS prefetch script is off; Speculation Rules (a JSON block in <head>) replace it. SPEC §2 / §6: formulas in $…$ and $$…$$, rendered to MathML only (no KaTeX CSS, fonts or JS). `unified()` keeps the remark/rehype pipeline that these plugins need. Get started, then the lessons by stage with their codes, then the project pages (src/lib/sidebar.ts). design/README.md §3: white mark on black by default, black mark on white for the light theme. The wordmark is the site title rendered beside the mark. SPEC §12: broken internal links and anchors fail the build. The link-preview card (Starlight already sets twitter:card to summary_large_image). Fonts are self-hosted (@fontsource) so no third-party request happens before consent. Code blocks follow the site theme only (never the OS scheme), on gray backgrounds. SPEC D9: dark by default, dark/light picker only. Les…

nodes.label: concept-aggregate-window.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data). Two metaphors, stacked so they fit a phone, 8 s loop of 8 phases. Aggregate, "many rows -> one answer": 1 three rows, each holding a value; 2 to 4 the values slide, one row at a time, into one spot; 5 the rows are gone and one Σ row stands; 6 its row count. Window function, "every row keeps its seat and gets a note": 1 the same rows; 2 to 4 arrows read the group into one Σ bubble; 5 to 7 a copy of Σ slides back to each row, one per phase; 8 hold. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const H = 140; // top of the second panel

nodes.label: concept-aggregate.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for aggregate functions. Metaphor: many rows go in, one number comes out. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 four rows with a value each; 2 to 5 one row per phase slides into the box (and is gone), COUNT ticks up by one and SUM adds that row's value; 6 to 8 hold: COUNT is 4, SUM is the total of x1 to x4, and a ring marks the two answers. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): over 10, NULL, 30 COUNT(*) is 3 and SUM is 40; an aggregate over many rows returns one row. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-ai-check.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for checking an AI-written query. Metaphor: a draft is not trusted until it passes checks. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 an AI draft query; 2 check 1 (row count) says ok; 3 check 2 (a total you already know) says differs; 4 the draft is not trusted ("fix it"); 5 the draft slides down to try again; 6 and 7 both checks say ok; 8 trusted. Facts: a process, not engine output. Checks named here are the ones the lesson teaches: a row count that makes sense for the question (a join that changes the count is the usual cause of a wrong total, see the fan-out figure) and a total you can confirm another way. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-case.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for CASE. Metaphor: each row walks down the WHEN tests; the first yes stops the walk. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 three rows wait; 2 all three step to WHEN 1 and 3 its verdict shows (Row 1 yes: gold and stops, label A; Rows 2 and 3 no: red); 4 Rows 2 and 3 step to WHEN 2 and 5 its verdict (Row 2 yes, label B; Row 3 no); 6 Row 3 steps to ELSE and 7 gets label C; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): CASE returns the result of the first WHEN that is true; a row whose test is NULL counts as not true and goes on (10, NULL, 30 with WHEN v>20 / WHEN v>5 / ELSE gave mid, other, hi); with no ELSE and no true test the result is NULL. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const ROWS = [['Row 1', 1, 'A'], ['Row 2', 2, 'B'], ['Row 3', 3, 'C']]; // row, the column it stops at, its label

nodes.label: concept-cohort.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for cohort tables. Metaphor: users grouped by the month they started; each row is read across, and later months fill in as a triangle. Rows Start 1, 2, 3 (cohorts); columns month 0, 1, 2 (months since the start). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the empty grid (dashed); 2 month 0 fills for every cohort; 3 month 1 slides out of month 0 for cohorts 1 and 2; 4 month 2 slides out for cohort 1; 5 the dashed corner is marked "not yet"; 6 to 8 hold, a triangle. Darker means more users. Facts: not SQL output; cohort 3 started last, so it has had no month 1 or 2 yet, and cohort 2 has had no month 2. That is why the table is a triangle, not a rectangle. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-conditional-agg.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for conditional aggregation. Metaphor: one pass over the rows fills several counters. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 five rows with keys A, B, A, C, A and three counters at 0; 2 to 6 one row per phase sends a dot to the counter whose condition it meets (the counter then ticks up); 7 and 8 hold: A 3, B 1, C 1, all from a single pass. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): over keys A, B, A, C, A, `SUM(CASE WHEN k = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)` is 3 and `COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE k = 'B')` is 1, in one SELECT over the table. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const CX = { A: 80, B: 180, C: 280 }; // counter centers const RX = (i) => 10 + 70 * i; // row chip x (centers are multiples of 10) const SEEN = { A: [3, 5, 7], B: [4], C: [6] }; // phase at which each tally appears

nodes.label: concept-confounder.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for study design, lesson C1. Metaphor: a gap between two groups, then a third thing that is tied to both the groups and the result and can explain the gap by itself. Generic words only (group, result, a third thing): the lesson's Predict about the stores is answered by data in the reveal, not here. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 two boxes, group (with groups A and B) and result, joined by a dashed arrow; 2 the result differs between A and B (hi and lo) and a ring marks the result box; 3 hold; 4 a third box appears; 5 an arrow is drawn from it to the group box; 6 an arrow is drawn from it to the result box; 7 and 8 a closing line: it can explain the gap by itself. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the boxes or arrows drawn at that phase and appears with it. the group and result boxes, each with its small chips the dashed arrow between them and its label, which changes with the phase the third thing and its two arrows, drawn one after the other

nodes.label: concept-constraints.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for table constraints. Metaphor: rows try to enter a table with rules; rows that break a rule bounce off. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the table with its three rules (NOT NULL, UNIQUE, CHECK) and five waiting rows; 2 Row 1 is fine and goes in; 3 Row 2 has a ? in a column that only has CHECK, and a ? passes CHECK, so it goes in; 4 Row 3 has no name and bounces off NOT NULL; 5 Row 4 repeats a key and bounces off UNIQUE; 6 Row 5 has a bad age and bounces off CHECK; 7 and 8 hold: two rows stored. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out), table (id PRIMARY KEY, name NOT NULL UNIQUE, age CHECK (age >= 0)): inserting a NULL name fails ("NOT NULL constraint failed"); a repeated name fails ("violates unique constraint"); age -1 fails ("CHECK constraint failed"); age NULL is accepted (a CHECK that evaluates to NULL passes); a failed INSERT stores nothing. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const ROWS = [['Row 1', 0], ['Row 2 · age ?', 0], ['Row 3 · no name', 4], ['Row 4 · repeat', 5], ['Row 5 · bad age', 6]]; // label, phase of the bounce (0 = goes in)

nodes.label: concept-coverage.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for confidence intervals (core lesson C7). Metaphor: a 95 percent interval is a recipe, and you judge a recipe by running it many times. One vertical ochre line is the true value (in real work it is unknown); each row is one sample's interval, a blue bar with a blue dot for its estimate. The offsets and widths are invented for the picture; the geometry asserts that exactly 1 of the 20 intervals misses the line. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 one interval; 2 three more; 3 six more; 4 and 5 ten more (20 in all); 6 the interval that misses the line turns red and is labeled; 7 a count, 19 of 20 cross, which is what a 95 percent recipe promises in the long run; 8 holds. Colors by meaning, the same in C5 to C7: ochre = the true value, blue = a sample's estimate and interval, red = a miss. the interval that misses is drawn blue until phase 6, then red

nodes.label: concept-cte-kinds.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data). Metaphor: a CTE is a named scratch table you plug into the next step. Three scenes are on the page from the start and take turns moving, 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 standalone: the CTE card slides into MAIN; 2 and 3 chained: the CTE 1 card slides into CTE 2, then CTE 2 (with CTE 1 inside) slides into MAIN; 4 and 5 recursive: a loop arrow draws and two new rows slide into the CTE that feeds itself; 6 it slides into MAIN; 7 and 8 hold. A soft ring pulses where something has just landed. Key idea only: no count strip, because the figure shows three structures, not rows to count. the title sits where no card passes: low in a wide box, high in the tall one standalone chained recursive: the card feeds itself two new rows, then plugs into MAIN

nodes.label: concept-date-trunc.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for DATE_TRUNC. Metaphor: a timestamp snaps down to the start of its month. Three lanes, each a calendar line with ticks at the start of March, April and May; each lane has one timestamp (a dot). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 three timestamps; 2, 3 and 4 the dots slide left, one lane per phase, to the first of their month; the result label appears the phase after; 6 t1 and t2 ended on the same value. The dot never moves right: the cut is always down. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out and facts2.out): date_trunc('month', timestamp '2024-03-17 14:05:00') = 2024-03-01 00:00:00; the last day of a month (Mar 29 23:59) also goes to the first of its own month, never to the next one. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. ]; // label, timestamp, dot x, tick x it snaps to, result

nodes.label: concept-dedup.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for removing duplicates with ROW_NUMBER. Metaphor: number the repeats of each key, keep #1. Five rows with keys A, B, A, B... as Row 1 A, Row 2 A, Row 3 B, Row 4 A, Row 5 B. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the rows; 2 the A rows are numbered #1, #2, #3; 3 the B rows are numbered #1, #2; 4 the #1 badges glow (keep); 5 the other rows turn red and are marked dropped; 6 and 7 the two kept rows slide into the clean table; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY k ORDER BY ts) gives A: 1, 2, 3 and B: 1, 2; WHERE rn = 1 keeps one row per key. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const ROWS = [['A', 1], ['A', 2], ['B', 1], ['A', 3], ['B', 2]]; // key, number within its key

nodes.label: concept-expression.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for expressions. Metaphor: two cells go in, a new cell comes out, on every row. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 two columns A and B; 2 to 4 on each row in turn copies of its A and B cells slide into the new column and 3 to 5 the computed cell "A × B" replaces them; 6 to 8 hold, every row has a new value and A and B are unchanged. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): an expression such as 2*3 gives 6 per row and leaves its source columns as they were. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-fanout.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for join fan-out. Metaphor: one row meets three, and becomes three, so a SUM counts it three times. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 one order row O1 with an amount a, and three item rows I1 to I3; 2 O1 matches all three (arrows); 3 to 5 the join makes one result row per match: each item slides into the result and gets a copy of O1's amount; 6 SUM(a) adds a three times; 7 a note: a is counted 3 times; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): orders (1, 10), (2, 20) joined to items (1,x), (1,y), (1,z), (2,x) give order 1 three times; SUM(amt) over the join is 50 while SUM(amt) over orders is 30. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const IY = (i) => 60 + 30 * i; // item row i in the top area const RY = (i) => 170 + 30 * i; // result row i

nodes.label: concept-funnel.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for a funnel. Metaphor: users drop out at every stage, so each bar is narrower than the one above. Four bars of users (n1 to n4). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 everyone at step 1; 2, 4 and 6 the users who go on slide down from the bar above to make the next, narrower bar; 3, 5 and 7 that bar gets its label and the dashed red outline shows the users who left. Facts: not SQL output; the rule shown is the usual funnel count, each step counts only users who also did the earlier steps, so n1 >= n2 >= n3 >= n4 by construction. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-group-by.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for GROUP BY and HAVING. Metaphor: sort rows into one bucket per key, then each bucket becomes one row. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 six rows, each tagged with a key (A, B, C); 2 the A rows slide into their bucket, 3 the B rows, 4 the C row; 5 each bucket becomes one row with its count; 6 HAVING drops a whole bucket (C, which holds one row); 7 and 8 hold. Live counters and Key idea (D41): counts are the rows drawn in the picture at that phase; each appears with its phase. const ROWS = [['A', 0], ['B', 0], ['A', 1], ['C', 0], ['B', 1], ['A', 2]]; // key, slot in its bucket the empty seats the rows leave behind, and the buckets the rows: each slides to its bucket slot, then is replaced by the bucket's single row the last row slides along its own line first and then up, so it never passes over the row above it

nodes.label: concept-index.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for indexes. Two stacked panels, 8 s loop of 8 phases. The same six rows, and the engine is looking for the rows with key K (r2 and r5). Top, a full scan: 1 to 6 a frame moves over the rows one by one, and each row it has read turns darker; 7 all six were read. Bottom, an index: 1 the index knows K is in r2 and r5; 2 arrows jump straight to those two rows; 3 only they are read, while the scan above is still crawling. 8 hold. Facts: an index lets the engine find matching rows without reading every row, but the engine decides whether using it pays off (DuckDB's docs give a selectivity guideline, not a rule, and the lesson run showed the engine using an index on a 355-row filter; see MISTAKES), so the picture says "can jump", not "always jumps". Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const P2 = 120; // top of the second panel

nodes.label: concept-join.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animations (SPEC D41, no real data), one per join type: `node scripts/make-animation.mjs concept-join:left` (variants inner, left, right, full, cross) and a cycling overview `concept-join:all`. Two small tables of labels, keys A B C and B C D. Metaphor: keys shake hands. 8 s loop of 8 phases for inner, left, right and full: 1 the tables; 2 the matching keys slide together and shake hands (violet); 3 each pair moves into the result; 4 the rows the join also keeps move in (with NULL cells), or are marked red and stay behind; 5 the row count; 6 to 8 hold. CROSS has no keys to match: every row meets every row, and every pairing is a result row, three at a time. `all` steps through LEFT, RIGHT, INNER and FULL, two phases each, with the type name lit. Every variant carries live counters, a Key idea and What changed (D41). Live counts (D41): the rows drawn at each phase, with a Key idea and What changed per step. The four keyed variants share steps 1 to 3 and differ in what they keep (step 4) and in the closing step. const Y = (i) => 44 + 30 * i; // row i of a source column or of the result the circles of kept keys (they count keys, not rows) the seats the rows leave behind the t…

nodes.label: concept-keys.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for primary and foreign keys. Metaphor: one parent row, many child rows pointing at it. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 table P, one unique key per row (PK); 2 table C, each row stores a P key (FK); 3 to 5 each FK arrow draws to its P row (C1 and C2 to P1, C3 to P2: one to many); 6 the "one to many" label; 7 a row C4 whose FK points at a P row that does not exist is marked red and refused; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): a PRIMARY KEY rejects a repeated or NULL value; inserting a child whose key has no parent fails ("Violates foreign key constraint because key does not exist in the referenced table"); a NULL foreign key is allowed. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const CH = [['C1', 'P1', 72, 92], ['C2', 'P1', 102, 92], ['C3', 'P2', 132, 152]]; // child, its FK, child center y, parent center y

nodes.label: concept-logical-order.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data): the logical order of a SQL query. Left: the clauses in the order they are written (SELECT first); the number beside each appears when it runs. Right: t1 and t2 combine into one table of seven rows, then each clause changes it, and the table shrinks. 8 s loop of 8 phases, one per clause: 1 FROM/JOIN/ON; 2 WHERE (two rows slide out, the rest close the gaps); 3 GROUP BY (the kept rows take their group's shade and a one-row-per-group table appears); 4 HAVING (group A slides out, the others move up); 5 SELECT (the output is chosen); 6 ORDER BY (a sort number appears); 7 LIMIT (the group that sorts second slides out); 8 hold. Live counters and Key idea (D41): counts are the rows drawn in the picture at that phase; each appears with its phase. const KEYS = ['A', 'A', 'B', 'B', 'B', 'C', 'C']; // group key of rows r1 to r7 const DROPPED = [1, 4]; // WHERE drops r2 and r5 const TY = 84; // top of the first table row const GY = 252; // top of the first group row written order, with the clause that runs in each phase lit t1 and t2 combine into one table the table: WHERE drops r2 and r5 (they slide out), the rows below close the gaps; GROUP BY shade…

nodes.label: concept-mean-median.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41) for center, lesson C2. A made-up miniature, labeled as such on the page: five orders of 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 dollars on a number line from 0 to 100, then a sixth, 100 (a 10 typed with an extra zero). Metaphor: the mean follows an extreme value, the median barely moves. Colors fixed across Part 1: mean = ochre dashed line, median = green solid line, the data = blue dots, the odd value = red. Facts (computed by hand, checked in Python): mean(10, 12, 14, 16, 18) = 14 and median = 14; mean(10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 100) = 170 / 6 = 28.33 and median = (14 + 16) / 2 = 15. Positions: x = 20 + 3.2 * dollars. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 five dots on the line; 2 the mean and the median lines are drawn, both at 14; 3 hold; 4 a sixth dot, 100, appears in red; 5 hold; 6 the mean and the median lines move to 28.33 and 15 (the old mean stays as a faint mark); 7 an arrow shows the mean's jump; 8 hold. The text row above the line changes from the first pair of values to the second. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the dots or values drawn at that phase and appears with it. const BASE = 118; // y of the number line the number line the lines first (under the d…

nodes.label: concept-natural-frequencies.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41) for Bayes with natural frequencies, lesson C4. A made-up miniature, labeled as such on the page (the lesson's own numbers are different): 1,000 orders drawn as 100 squares of 10 orders each; 100 orders hold a mistake (10 squares); a check flags 8 in 10 of the mistakes (80) and 1 in 10 of the 900 correct orders (90). Flagged = 80 real mistakes + 90 false alarms = 170. Colors fixed across Part 1: the data (correct orders) blue, the thing sought (mistakes) ochre, flagged red. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the grid of 100 squares and its label; 2 the top row turns ochre: 100 mistakes, 900 correct; 3 hold; 4 the flagged squares get a red edge (8 in the mistake row, 9 among the others); 5 hold; 6 a bar of the 170 flagged orders appears, 80 real and 90 false alarms; 7 and 8 hold. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the number drawn at that phase and appears with it. const P = 16; // pitch of a square const FLAGGED_OTHERS = [[1, 2], [2, 5], [3, 7], [4, 0], [5, 4], [6, 8], [7, 3], [8, 6], [9, 1]]; // [row, column] of the 9 flagged correct orders' squares const PX = 182; // left of the right-hand panel the grid: one fill, the mistake row on top of it,…

nodes.label: concept-normalize.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for normalization. Metaphor: a repeating part moves out into its own table, stored once, and a key links the two. One wide table with columns id, key, info; the info repeats for every row with the same key (A, A, B, A). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the wide table; 2 the info column glows (it repeats); 3 the first info of each key slides into a new table and the repeats turn red; 4 the repeats are gone and the new table gets its keys; 5 arrows link each row's key to its info row; 6 to 8 hold. Facts: a design pattern, not engine output: after the split each fact about a key (here its info) is stored once and rows refer to it by key, so a change is made in one place; a join on the key puts the wide table back together. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-null.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for NULL. Metaphor: a ? is "no value here", not a value you can compare with. Two stacked panels, 8 s loop of 8 phases. Top, asking about the ?: 1 three cells x1, ?, x3; 2 and 3 the test `= NULL` answers ? for every row (the ? never equals anything, not even itself); 4 and 5 `IS NULL` answers no, yes, no. Bottom, SUM: 6 and 7 x1 and x3 flow into the sum while the ? is skipped; 8 the sum is x1 + x3. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): over 10, NULL, 30: `v = NULL` gives NULL on every row, `v IS NULL` gives false, true, false; `SUM(v)` = 40 (the NULL is skipped), `COUNT(*)` = 3, `COUNT(v)` = 2. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const H = 150; // top of the second panel

nodes.label: concept-query.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for what a query is. Metaphor: ask a question, get a table back. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 a table of four rows; 2 the question box lights up; 3 copies of the rows slide into the box (the table itself stays); 4 two rows come out inside the box; 5 they slide out into a new, smaller table; 6 to 8 hold with the row counts. Facts: a SELECT never changes the table it reads (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts2.out: SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > 5 returns 8 and 9, and the table still has all four rows afterwards). Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-rank-ties.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for ROW_NUMBER, RANK and DENSE_RANK on tied values. Metaphor: the same podium, three ways to number it. Rows sorted by score 9, 8, 8, 7 (the middle two tie). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the rows; 2 to 3 ROW_NUMBER numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 (two rows at a time); 4 to 5 RANK gives 1, 2, 2, 4 (skips 3); 6 to 7 DENSE_RANK gives 1, 2, 2, 3 (no gap); 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out), scores 90, 80, 80, 70 with ORDER BY score DESC: row_number 1,2,3,4; rank 1,2,2,4; dense_rank 1,2,2,3. ROW_NUMBER gives tied rows an arbitrary order unless the ORDER BY has a tie-breaker (here: the name). Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. ]; // name, center x, numbers, note, phase it starts

nodes.label: concept-recursive.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for a recursive CTE. Metaphor: round after round, the newest rows find the next rows, until a round finds none. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the anchor row waits in the "new rows" box; 2 it joins the result; 3 round 1 finds two rows (an arrow reads from the result); 4 they join the result; 5 round 2 finds one row; 6 it joins the result; 7 round 3 finds nothing, so it stops; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): WITH RECURSIVE r(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM r WHERE n < 3) returns 1, 2, 3: the anchor first, then each round builds on the previous round's rows, and it ends when a round returns no rows. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-sampling-distribution.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for the sampling distribution of the mean (core lesson C6). Metaphor: every sample turns into one number, its mean, and the pile of those numbers has a center and a width. Dots are schematic, not cafe-sales values. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 a sample of n orders (a row of dots, a bigger dot is a bigger order); 2 its mean, a blue dot, drops onto the axis; 3 and 4 two more samples, two more means; 5 and 6 the pile fills up (16 means in all) and the ochre line marks the true mean at its center; 7 a second axis shows a bigger n: the same number of means in a much narrower pile; 8 holds. Colors by meaning, the same in C5 to C7: ochre = the true value, blue = a sample's estimate. The offsets are multiples of 10 px from the center, so a column is a stack of dots 10 px apart; the 16 means of n = 5 are wide, those of n = 20 narrow. const OFF5 = [-30, 20, 0, -10, 40, 10, -20, 0, 20, -40, 10, 30, 0, -10, 10, 0]; // pile of means, small n const OFF20 = [0, -10, 0, 10, 0, 0, -20, 10, 0, -10, 20, 10, 0, 10, -10, 20]; // pile of means, large n const ROWS = [[4, 7, 5, 8, 3], [6, 3, 8, 5, 6], [5, 8, 4, 6, 7]]; // dot radius of the five orders in each of the…

nodes.label: concept-sampling.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for samples and bias (core lesson C5). Metaphor: a sample can only speak for the cases it could reach. A population of 24 orders as dots (a bigger dot is a bigger order), drawn in 8 columns, the 2 left columns being the mornings. The marks are schematic, not cafe-sales values. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the population and its true mean (ochre line on the value axis); 2 and 3 six orders are drawn at random (blue rings, spread over the columns); 4 their mean lands on the axis, close to the true mean (blue dot); 5 and 6 the rings go and the six morning orders are drawn instead (the gray band is the easy-to-reach corner); 7 their mean lands far to the left, and a red bracket marks the gap to the true mean; 8 holds. Colors by meaning, the same in C5 to C7: ochre = the true value, blue = a sample's estimate, red = a miss. The values below are invented for the picture; the geometry asserts that the random draw lands near the true mean and the morning draw does not. ]; // value of the order in each column, rows 0 to 2 const RANDOM = [[1, 1], [2, 0], [3, 2], [4, 1], [5, 0], [7, 2]]; // [column, row] of the six random orders const xv = (v) => 30 + ((v…

nodes.label: concept-select-order-limit.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for SELECT, ORDER BY and LIMIT. Metaphor: pick, deal out in order, keep the top. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 a table of four rows with columns A, B, C (B is the sort key); 2 SELECT keeps columns A and B, C fades; 3 to 6 ORDER BY deals the rows one at a time into a new table, smallest key first (r2, r4, r1, r3), each sliding on its own phase so no two rows cross; 7 LIMIT 2 draws a cut line under the second slot; 8 the rows below it fade, the top 2 stay. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts2.out): the engine sorts first and LIMIT then keeps the first rows of the sorted result. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const ROWS = [['r1', 3, 'c1', 2, 5], ['r2', 1, 'c2', 0, 3], ['r3', 4, 'c3', 3, 6], ['r4', 2, 'c4', 1, 4]]; // id, key, C value, slot in the sorted table, phase it moves

nodes.label: concept-self-join.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for the self join. Metaphor: one table used twice, under two nicknames (aliases). A table T has four rows, each storing the number of another row of T as its "boss". 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 table T; 2 a copy of its rows slides to the right; 3 the two copies are named T AS e and T AS b; 4 to 6 each row of e gets paired with its boss row in b (Row 2 and Row 3 to Row 1, Row 4 to Row 2); 7 Row 1 has no boss, so it has no pair; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): emp(id, boss) = (1, NULL), (2, 1), (3, 1), (4, 2); emp e JOIN emp b ON e.boss = b.id gives (2, 1), (3, 1), (4, 2); row 1, whose boss is NULL, has no pair. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const PAIR = [[1, 0], [2, 0], [3, 1]]; // e row, b row

nodes.label: concept-set-ops.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for the set operators. Metaphor: two lists of keys as two circles; each operator lights up its own part, and its result list appears. Set 1 holds keys A, B, C; set 2 holds B, C, D (B and C are in both). 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the two sets; 2 UNION lights everything and 3 its list A B C D appears; 4 INTERSECT lights the overlap and 5 its list B C; 6 EXCEPT lights what is only in set 1 and 7 its list A; 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): UNION gives A, B, C, D (repeats removed; UNION ALL would give B and C twice); INTERSECT gives B, C; set 1 EXCEPT set 2 gives A (set 2 EXCEPT set 1 would give D, so the order matters). Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-shard.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for sharding. Metaphor: one big table is split into shards by key, so a query for one key visits one shard. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 one table of five rows with keys A, B, C, A, B; 2 the A rows slide into shard A; 3 the B rows into shard B; 4 the C row into shard C; 5 a query for key B appears and its arrow points at shard B; 6 shard B lights up, the other two are marked not visited; 7 and 8 hold. Facts: a design idea, not a DuckDB feature (DuckDB runs on one machine; sharding spreads a table across machines in other systems): the shard is chosen from the key, so a query that names the key can skip the other shards, while a query that does not name it must ask every shard. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const ROWS = [['A', 0], ['B', 0], ['C', 0], ['A', 1], ['B', 1]]; // key, slot in its shard

nodes.label: concept-sliding-window.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for a sliding window frame and LAG. Metaphor: a frame of three rows slides down the ordered rows and each row gets the average of what is inside it; LAG reads the row above. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 four ordered rows and the frame on row 1 (the two seats above row 1 are empty, dashed); 2 to 4 the frame slides down one row per phase; the average of each stop appears the phase after (x1, x1..x2, x1..x3, x2..x4); 6 to 8 LAG shows, per row, the value of the row above (none, x1, x2, x3). Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out), v = 2, 4, 6, 8, 10: avg(v) OVER (ORDER BY i ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) is 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 8.0 (the first rows average fewer rows); lag(v) OVER (ORDER BY i) is NULL, 2, 4, 6, 8. Live counters and Key idea (D41): counts are the rows drawn in the picture at that phase; each appears with its phase. The counters count what is drawn: rows in the frame (1, 2, 3, 3), averages shown (x1 from the start, then one per phase), LAG values shown.

nodes.label: concept-split-apply-combine.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for pandas groupby. Metaphor: split the rows into one group per key, apply one calculation to each group, combine the results into a new table. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 six rows, each tagged with a key (A, B, C); 2 the A rows slide into their group, 3 the B rows, 4 the C row (split); 5 each group becomes one row with its count (apply); 6 the three result rows get a blue edge together and a "new table" label, the combine step; 7 and 8 hold. Same geometry as concept-group-by (checked for overlap there); the only differences are the words and the phase 6 edge. Live counters and Key idea (D41): counts are the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase; each appears with its phase. const ROWS = [['A', 0], ['B', 0], ['A', 1], ['C', 0], ['B', 1], ['A', 2]]; // key, slot in its group the empty seats the rows leave behind, and the groups the rows: each slides to its group slot, then is replaced by the group's single row the last row slides along its own line first and then up, so it never passes over the row above it combine: the three result rows get a blue edge together, and a label above the groups names them a table

nodes.label: concept-star.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for the star schema. Metaphor: a fact table in the middle, dimension tables around it, each joined by one key. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the fact table alone; 2, 3, 4 and 5 the dimension tables A, B, C and D slide in from outside, one per phase; 3, 4, 5 and 6 the key link to each one draws the phase after it arrives; 7 a ring marks the star; 8 hold. Facts: a modeling pattern, not engine output: the fact table holds one row per event with a key to each dimension, and a query joins the fact table to the dimensions it needs, one join per dimension. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. name, final x, final y, move dx, dy, link path, key label x, y

nodes.label: concept-subquery.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for a subquery. Metaphor: the inner query answers first, and its answer feeds the outer one. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the outer query has four rows (3, 8, 2, 9) and an empty slot in its test "x >"; the inner query box says AVG(x); 2 the inner query runs and produces one value v; 3 v slides down into the empty slot; 4 the outer query now has its test; 5 the rows are tested against v: 3 and 2 fail (red), 8 and 9 stay; 6 to 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out and facts2.out): SELECT x FROM t WHERE x > (SELECT AVG(x) FROM t) over 3, 8, 2, 9 gives 8 and 9 (the average is 5.5); the inner query is evaluated first and gives one value. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-text-clean.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for cleaning text. Metaphor: a chain of small clean-ups, one function at a time. The · stands for a space. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the messy text in its chip; 2 the chip slides down to TRIM and 3 its text is "Iced··Tea"; 4 it slides to REPLACE and 5 the double space becomes one; 6 it slides to LOWER and 7 the text is "iced·tea"; 8 hold. Each step the chip leaves behind a dimmed copy of the text it had, so the whole chain shows at the end. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): TRIM(' Iced Tea ') = 'Iced Tea' (only the ends), REPLACE(…, ' ', ' ') = 'Iced Tea', LOWER(…) = 'iced tea'. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-transaction.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for transactions. Two stacked panels with the same start, 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 a table with one row; 2 BEGIN: change 1 waits (dashed: not final); 3 change 2 waits; 4 the stamp COMMIT (top) or ROLLBACK (bottom); 5 top: both changes slide into the table together; bottom: both are undone together; 6 top: they are solid rows; 7 and 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): on a table with row 1, BEGIN; INSERT 2; INSERT 3; ROLLBACK; leaves only row 1, and the same with COMMIT leaves rows 1, 2, 3. Outside an explicit transaction ROLLBACK is an error in DuckDB ("cannot rollback - no transaction is active"), so ROLLBACK only makes sense after BEGIN. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it. const H = 160; // top of the second panel

nodes.label: concept-view.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for views. Metaphor: a view is a saved question, not saved answers: ask it again after the data changed and the answer is fresh. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 a table t with two rows and a view v (a saved query) on it; 2 you ask FROM v, and the arrows draw from t through v; 3 the answer is built from t right now (Σ of two rows); 4 a new row arrives in t; 5 the view runs again (ring); 6 the answer changes to include the new row; 7 and 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): CREATE VIEW vw AS SELECT SUM(v) s FROM base; with base = 1, 2 SELECT * FROM vw gives 3; after INSERT INTO base VALUES (10) the same SELECT gives 13. The view stored the query, not the result. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the rows or items drawn in the picture at that phase, and appears with it.

nodes.label: concept-where.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41, no real data) for WHERE. Metaphor: a gate that lets a row through only when the test is true. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 four rows with a value x (9, 3, ?, 7; ? is NULL); 2 the gate "WHERE x > 5" appears; 3 to 6 one row per phase is tested: its verdict shows and it either slides through (true) or stops at the gate in red (false, or unknown for the ?); 7 and 8 hold. Facts (DuckDB 2.0.0, concept2/facts.out): `WHERE v > 15` over 10, NULL, 30 keeps only 30, so the NULL row is dropped like a false one; a row is kept only when the condition is true. Live counters and Key idea (D41): counts are the rows drawn in the picture at that phase; each appears with its phase.

nodes.label: concept-z-score.mjs
nodes.text: Concept animation (SPEC D41) for the z-score, lesson C3. A made-up miniature, labeled as such on the page: a column with mean 40 and standard deviation 10, and one value x = 60. Positions: x = 20 + 4 * value on the value line, and the z line below uses the same pixels, so z = 2 sits under 60 (z = 0 at the mean, 40; one step of z is 40 px). Facts: 60 - 40 = 20; 20 / 10 = 2. 8 s loop of 8 phases: 1 the value line with its mean, a bracket for one standard deviation, and the value x = 60; 2 an arrow from the mean to x is drawn and labeled x - mean = 20; 3 hold; 4 the line "20 / 10 = 2 standard deviations" appears; 5 hold; 6 the z line appears under the value line, with a dashed drop from x; 7 the point z = 2 appears on it; 8 hold. Live counters and Key idea (D41): each counter shows the number drawn at that phase and appears with it. const AX = 96; // y of the value line const ZY = 198; // y of the z line the value line with ticks and labels the mean, one SD, and the value subtract: an arrow from the mean to x, with its label divide the z line below, aligned with the value line

nodes.label: sql-group-by-having.mjs
nodes.text: S8 GROUP BY and HAVING: ten real orders (1719 to 1728 of cafe-sales v1), five steps the learner advances one at a time: input rows, GROUP BY shades them by store, they gather into one bucket per store, each bucket collapses to one row with COUNT(*), HAVING drops the small group. Parts only fade in at their own slot, so text never overlaps at any moment. Checked with DuckDB 2.0.0: SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_id BETWEEN 1719 AND 1728 GROUP BY store_id gives store 2: 5, store 1: 3, store 3: 2; with HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3 it gives stores 2 and 1 (3 groups, 2 after HAVING). Each step also sets live counters (rows 10, groups 3, after HAVING 2), a Key idea and What changed (D41); a count appears at the step that shows it, so step 1 gives nothing of the Predict away. order_id, store_id in the order they were placed const STORES = [2, 1, 3]; // bucket order, biggest first const SHADE = { 1: tint('grp', 1), 2: tint('grp', 2), 3: tint('grp', 4) }; // three shades of the GROUP BY hue the input: ten rows that stay where they are; GROUP BY shades them at step 2 the buckets (step 3): one chip per order, in placement order the result (step 4); HAVING dims store 3 (step 5)

nodes.label: sql-inner-join.mjs
nodes.text: S19 INNER JOIN: the 7 order_items lines of orders 1001 to 1003 against 5 of the 16 products of cafe-sales v1, five steps the learner advances one at a time: the two tables, ON matches product 1, then 6, then 10 and 15, then product 16 has nothing to pair with. The result is drawn grouped by product so each match appends rows in one block (a join promises no row order). Parts only fade in at their own slot, so text never overlaps at any moment. Checked with DuckDB 2.0.0: order_items JOIN products ON product_id for order_id 1001 to 1003 returns 7 rows; products 1, 6 and 10 pair twice, 15 once, 16 never (result rows 2, 4, 7 after products 1, 6, 10 and 15). Live counters, a Key idea and What changed per step (D41); each shows only at its own step, so step 1 gives nothing of the Predict away. order_item_id, product_id const STEP = { 1: 2, 6: 3, 10: 4, 15: 4, 16: 5 }; // the step at which each key is matched (or found unmatched) const SHADE = { 1: tint('mat', 1), 6: tint('mat', 2), 10: tint('mat', 3), 15: tint('mat', 4) }; // four shades of the ON hue const frame = (step) => ({ in: step, ...(step < 5 ? { hide: step + 1 } : {}) }); // shown in its own step only (the last stays) a frame m…

nodes.label: sql-window-functions.mjs
nodes.text: S14 window functions: stores 1 and 2, January 1 to 3 of cafe-sales v1 (the lesson's own day-by-store rows), four steps the learner advances one at a time: six rows, GROUP BY collapses them to two, PARTITION BY shades the six, the window value fills in beside each. Parts only fade in at their own slot, so text never overlaps at any moment. Checked with DuckDB 2.0.0 (completed orders per store and day): store 1: 2, 3, 3 (total 8); store 2: 2, 4, 3 (total 9); GROUP BY store_id gives 2 rows, SUM(orders) OVER (PARTITION BY store_id) keeps all 6. Live counters (rows after each clause), a Key idea and What changed per step (D41); each shows only at its own step. const LEVEL = { 1: 1, 2: 3 }; // two shades of one hue the six rows; PARTITION BY shades them at step 3, the window column joins at step 4 the GROUP BY result, step 2

nodes.label: step-animation.mjs
nodes.text: Generator for learner-controlled step-by-step figures in lessons (SPEC D41). A spec draws the FINAL frame with ordinary shapes (so print and any browser that ignores the controls show it), then gives each part that changes an effect (`fx`), counted in steps from 1 (step 1 is the default view): in:n appears at step n (before it, invisible) out:n dimmed from step n on (a dropped row or group) hide:n invisible from step n on (a highlight that only marks one step: in:n, hide:n+1) Steps are `{ role, clause, text, predict? }`: `clause` is the badge text (GROUP BY, ON, ...), `role` picks its color (src mat flt grp out win ord, see src/styles/step-animation.css and LESSON-STANDARD.md), `predict` is an optional "Predict:" prompt for the step that comes next, which must not give away what that step reveals. Everything is a class from the stylesheet; the output has no style attribute, no script and no CSS variable. The controls are a native radio group with labels (no JavaScript), so keyboard arrows and JS-off both work. Concept primitives (on top of the table ones: row, rect, text, path): venn({ x1, x2, y, r }) two overlapping circles; `.outline()`, `.region('L'|'O'|'R', c, fx)` (left only,…

nodes.label: Cheatsheet
nodes.text: A one-page stage cheatsheet (SPEC D44), reusable: it renders any `Cheatsheet` from `src/data/cheatsheets/`. Each entry is a card with the pattern, one plain sentence, the most common trap and a link to the lesson that teaches it; the small figures sit beside their lesson. Plain HTML and CSS: no script, so it reads with JavaScript off. A phone gets one column, a wide screen several; print gets a compact grid on two A4 sheets, black on white, with no site chrome. The published English lessons of this stage by slug, and of the SQL stage for the "Next" lines. A lesson that is not in the collection (a fixture build, a draft) renders without its link: the unit test `tests/cheatsheet.test.ts` makes sure every cited lesson is published. The lesson code in lowercase is the id of the first card of each lesson (`#s8`); the lesson footers link to it (D44). One sentence under each drawing, in words, so color and shape are never the only cue. Wider than a lesson column so that two or three cards sit side by side; one column on phones. Cards fill each column top to bottom, so the sheet reads down the columns. Arriving from a lesson footer (#s8): calm outline in the site tokens, clear of the stic…

nodes.label: CheatsheetFigure
nodes.text: The small drawings of the stage cheatsheets (SPEC D44). SQL: the order a query runs its clauses, the join types, and aggregate against window. Excel: a messy sheet against a tidy table, a lookup as a key-matched join, and a pivot as rows collapsing into groups (numbers from the lessons E1, E5 and E8). Our own drawings, built at build time as inline SVG: no script, no image file. Colors are the clause roles of D41 (the same seven hues as `src/styles/step-animation.css`); text and outlines use the site tokens, so it reads in dark and light, and in print everything turns black on white. Every drawing has a title, a description and a caption in words, so color is never the only cue. ---- 1. The logical execution order ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---- 2. Join types ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---- 3. Aggregate against window ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---- 4. nodes.label: Term

Where interest invokers exist (Chromium) hover or keyboard focus on the link opens it (`interestfor`); elsewhere (Safari, Firefox) a small "?" button opens it by tap or click (`popovertarget`). Both dismiss with Esc or an outside click. No JS. The definition is also linked with aria-describedby. Unique per use, even when a term repeats on a page. Tap/click toggle for browsers without interest invokers. The 24 px target (WCAG 2.5.8) is built Anchored below the link by the browser; no gap, so the pointer can move onto the tip.

nodes.label: Careers
nodes.text: 05: pick a direction. The four careers (SPEC D32) from the owner-approved mockup, then the quiz teaser. Without script every career's details are shown in full, one after another, and each card is a link to its details: nothing is hidden and there is no figure. With script (scripts/home/careers.ts, no GSAP, every reader) the links become buttons (aria-expanded, aria-controls) that open one detail panel at a time, Data Analyst first. CSS draws that state from the first paint where script runs, so nothing moves when it arrives; `.is-static` (set when the chunk fails) brings back the full list. The looping canvas figure on the left of the panel is a deferred chunk loaded when the section nears (scripts/home/careers-figures.ts). "Not sure which *career fits you?*": the starred part is the muted second voice. Each panel's button (SPEC D37): the career's own first published lesson once its lessons are built ("Go to Data Analyst"), else the very first lesson ("Start at E1"), else /start/. Drafts never count.

The cards are one <ol> in DOM order. By default (no script, reduced motion, a blocked or failed chunk) they are a horizontal scroll-snap list. The deferred chunk (scripts/home/sections/history.ts) sets .is-live on the gallery: CSS then draws the slider's first frame (1804 centered; --d is a card's distance from the center, --s its scale, --o its opacity, from scripts/home/history-curve.ts like the GSAP loop), and the chunk builds the seamless loop, drag (Draggable), the buttons, ←/→ and the live region on it. nodes.label: Consent
nodes.text: Consent card + Consent Mode v2 + GA4 loader (SPEC §11, D8). Renders nothing, and so adds no HTML, CSS or JavaScript, while GA_ID is empty. When set: defaults are `denied` before anything loads, gtag.js is requested only after Accept, and the choice lives in localStorage `dfz-consent` ('granted' or 'denied'). Layout follows the owner's own site (johnha.info): a glass card floating at the bottom (bottom-left on wide screens), always above the taskbar, with Reject all / Accept all of equal weight and a Customize panel. Consent Mode v2: everything denied until the visitor accepts. Nothing is requested yet. s.src = 'https://www.googletagmanager.com/gtag/js?id=' + encodeURIComponent(id); {/* Inline and inside the condition: no stylesheet request at all while analytics is off. */} The taskbar's open menu always wins: the card steps aside until it closes. Short screens (landscape phones, 400% zoom): the card scrolls inside itself, never off screen. Docs pages: the sidebar owns the left edge, so the card starts at the content column.

nodes.label: gsap.ts
nodes.text: Single entry to GSAP for the homepage. Imported only from the deferred motion chunks, so the library never sits on the critical path. Plugins are registered by the modules that use them. No ticker.fps() cap and the default lagSmoothing: the ticker follows requestAnimationFrame, so tweens run at the display's refresh rate (120 Hz phones included). The brand ease: the same curve as `--ease` in home.css (the CSS intro), so a CSS entrance and a GSAP one land identically. Used as 'dfz' by every section. The mobile address bar resizing the viewport must not trigger a refresh while scrolling. Read-before-write for a batch of targets. GSAP reads an element's computed transform the first time it animates it, and every read after a write forces a style recalculation. Priming the caches of all targets first turns N interleaved read/write pairs into N reads in a row (one recalculation) followed by pure writes. / Run a timeline to its end and back to where it was. GSAP reads a tween's start values (computed styles, SVG path lengths) the first time it renders, which for a scrubbed timeline would be mid-scroll, in a frame the reader sees; this does it now, in a setup slot. nodes.label: history-curve.ts
nodes.text: The history slider's look as a function of a card's distance from the center (in cards), shared by the CSS first frame (components/home/History.astro, built at build time) and the GSAP loop (sections/history.ts), so the two always agree. No GSAP here: this module is also imported at build time. Cards move 80% of their width per step; one card's whole pass (400% → -400%) is ±5 steps. Opacity by distance, at |d| = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Scale and opacity are separate: the neighbors at ±1 stay at 0.9, so their smallest text (--soft) keeps 4.5:1 in both themes (dark about 7:1, light about 5.4:1); from ±2 the cards fade out. / u: 1 at the center, 0 at the ends of the pass (|d| = 5). The same two values for a whole-card distance (the CSS first frame).

nodes.label: motion.ts
nodes.text: Deferred homepage motion: nav, scroll progress, hero scroll-out, pointer effects, and the section timelines. Everything is inside gsap.matchMedia(), so reduced motion gets none of it (and in practice never even loads this chunk). Frame budget (SPEC §12, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz): per-frame work is O(1) and touches only transform and opacity. Sizes are measured once and again on ScrollTrigger's refresh, never inside a tween, and writes happen in GSAP's own rAF tick. Setup work (the section timelines) is split into one task per section and runs right after a presented frame, first for sections near the screen, then, while the reader is not scrolling, for the rest, so scrolling never pays for it. The history list (04) keeps the slider's height while it waits for its chunk: if the chunk cannot build the slider, the list takes its own height again. `all` also resets a slider whose setup failed halfway. / One unit of setup work: a section's init, or one of the later steps it asked for (see SectionInit). Resolves in the first task after the next frame's rendering: requestAnimationFrame runs before the frame's style, layout and paint, and the timeout fires after them. A step started here gets a fresh frame budget. (scheduler.yield() alone resumes before the next render, so a chain of yields still adds up to one long animation frame.) /

Every rule below was run against DuckDB-Wasm 1.32.0 (the message text is quoted in tests/sql-errors.test.ts); a message that matches no rule gets no tip, never a guess. First line of the engine message ("Parser Error:" and the like removed). Edit distance, to tell a typo ("store_nme") from a different word ("Oakland"). Binder Error: Referenced column "x" not found in FROM clause! / Candidate bindings: "a", "b" Catalog Error: Table with name x does not exist! / Did you mean "stores"? Binder Error: column "city" must appear in the GROUP BY clause or must be part of an aggregate function. Binder Error: Ambiguous reference to column name "store_id" (use: "s.store_id" or "o.store_id") Binder Error: No function matches the given name and argument types 'sum(VARCHAR)'. Conversion Error: Could not convert string 'abc' to INT32

nodes.label: sql-runtime.ts
nodes.text: SPEC D42: the DuckDB-Wasm engine behind <RunSQL>. This chunk is imported in the background once a block nears the viewport (or on first focus or Run with Data Saver), never earlier. Everything is self-hosted (the files in dist/_astro): no CDN, no request to a third party, no storage. One database per page; every block shares it, so a table or view made in one block is seen by the next. The same five tables, columns and types as datasets/cafe-sales/v1/cafe-sales.sql (no keys or constraints there). `types` is positional, so the header row still names the columns. Column names; empty for a statement that returns nothing (CREATE, DROP, SET...). Display text per cell, first `shown` rows only; `null` is SQL NULL. Right-aligned columns (numbers). Where loading stands, for the progress line: `fraction` is 0..1 while the engine downloads. The engine file is 34,242,586 bytes raw (duckdb-eh.wasm of the pinned 1.32.0); the server sends it gzipped, and the download reports decoded bytes, so the bar divides by the raw size when the reported total is the smaller gzip size.
